The need for improving flexibility, optimality, and transparency of industry processes increases since the  customer demands are highly  diverse and full of uncertainty. CyberPhysical System (CPS) technology now is being developed to meet those requirements. It can be achieved through Digital Twin (DT). Unfortunately, the application of DT is still limited in practice nowadays, and no standard way to achieve integration. The concept of an Asset Administration Shell (AAS) proposed by Plattform Industrie 4.0 arose as a promising concept to realize DT in standard manner. However, the granularity of AAS remains undefined and still  under development. A literature study shows that most of studies only reached static digital twin and only considered a few specific assets especially unmovable assets. Dynamic digital twin is only supported by Virtual Reality (VR) that cannot be used for optimization as well as direct controlling. Therefore, this research intends to contribute to DT development by  proposing 3D  computer simulation technology as  dynamic digital  twin  by  following Reference Architecture Model Industrie 4.0 (RAMI  4.0) based on AAS  Framework. The proposed concept enables DT to do dynamic monitoring, optimization, and direct controlling. As a use case, a smart warehouse in Taiwan is used and assets considered include Automated Guided Vehicles (AGVs), Operator, Conveyor, Forklift, and Storage Rack. This research consists of 4 stages. First, AAS Variables Definition, identifying the assets and the data that want to be exchanged via AAS, defining AAS capability and AAS structure. Second, AAS Simulation Modeling with Flexsim software is established. Third, AAS System Integration consists  of  designing  communication  networks  and  information  modeling.  And  last, demonstrating  2  main  advantages  of  using  simulation  which  are simulation-based optimization  for  AGV  capacity  planning  and  creating  dynamic  dashboard. To  support communication between assets,  OPC  Unified Architecture  (OPC  UA)  and  Automation Markup  Language  (AutomationML)  are  determined.  As  a  result  of  demonstration, simulation-based optimization is done for multi-objectives and can find the optimum capacity of each AGV. Dynamic dashboard is also created to ease real-time monitoring process. Later on, data from dashboard can be exported to database and predictive analytics can be done. Based on these  capabilities, industry 4.0 scenarios can be  integrated  systematically and comprehensively.
Keywords : Asset Administration Shell, Digital Twin, Simulation, Optimization

In discussing Industry 4.0, there is a framework that approaches the issue of Industry 4.0 in a structured manner, namely Reference Architecture Model for Industry 4.0 (RAMI 4.0) proposed by German Plattform Industrie 4.0 shown in Figure 2.1 [5]. Actually, there are also other frameworks with the same purpose like Industrial Internet Reference Architecture (IIRA) proposed by IIC from US  [20], IBM  Industry 4.0 Architecture proposed by IBM [21], and NIST Smart Manufacturing [22].

Compared to others,  RAMI  4.0  gives  more comprehensive information and  more relevant to be implemented in industry especially for smart manufacturing [21]. RAMI 4.0 provides an orientation for plotting the requirements of sectors together with standards in order to define and further develop Industry 4.0 [23]. It is implemented in Industry 4.0 aspects for smart manufacturing which combines all elements and IT components [24].

Since the main challenge of industry 4.0 is interoperability, it is also shown in RAMI 4.0 from architectural layers which are divided into 2 aspects, namely physical aspects and digital  aspects. The  physical thing  is  called an  asset, while  the  digital  aspect  starts  from communication layers until business layers as shown in Figure 2.1. To change the physical thing  to the digital,  there is  integration layer between asset and communication layers that applies the Digital Twin (DT) concept.
Figure 2. 1 Reference Architecture Model for Industry 4.0
Figure 2. 1 Reference Architecture Model for Industry 4.0

The concept of the Digital  Twin (DT)  came from the presentation in 2002 entitled 'Conceptual Ideal for Product Lifecycle Management (PLM)' by Dr. Grieves [25]. It is called 'Twin' because it is like mirroring or twinning of systems between what existed in real space to what existed in virtual space and vice versa. But at that time, internet was still expensive and limited. Since DT uses internet as the basic technology so that the development of DT did not appear. But  today, internet becomes cheaper and borderless so  that  many industries have implemented DT to enhance interoperability across value stream of an asset like  shown in Figure 2.2 [26].

The concept of DT will be different with the other modeling concept even others show like mirroring the physical system. For example, Computer Aided Manufacturing (CAM) is also mirroring the physical system but it does not have capability to connect physical system with digital  system with bi-directional. This is the main difference of DT concept compared with others. In DT, digital system will be connected in real-time and have capability to control physical system. However, CAM or others concept can also be applied as part of DT.
Figure 2. 2 Development of Digital Twin in 2015
Figure 2. 2 Development of Digital Twin in 2015

Digital twin (DT) is known as the basic concept to support integration in Industry 4.0 and refers to virtual models of an asset that are fully integrated with a real thing/asset [27].  In DT, digital asset and physical asset are connected by internet with semantic relationships. It can be used for virtual testing, analyzing collected data, and predicting future behavior of physical things before applying it to real things [15]. Since DT has so many advantages, DT can be practically applied in almost every industry like shown in Table 2.1.

Besides that, DT also can solve information silos problems as shown in Figure  2.3. Traditionally, the information about an asset is usually scattered across multiple information sources,  which  are  maintained  by  different  organizations.  It will  result  in  du plicated, inconsistent, and missing information. With digital twin, it can collect data centrally for every entity and then makes that information available to different areas of the business for their specific  applications  through  integration  interfaces,  such  as  Application  Programming Interfaces (APIs) [29]. This improves decision-making through a shared understanding and reduces the overall lifecycle cost of operating and maintaining a plant.
Figure 2. 3 Digital Twin to Solve Information Silos Problem

One of the approaches to realize Digital Twin in manufacturing industry is called Asset Administration Shell (AAS) [29]. AAS basically consists of two terms which are 'Asset' and 'Administration Shell'.  The  asset  refers  to  the  physical  things  e.g.  machine, product, & materials, and the administration shell refers to the digital thing that stores information about the asset over its  entire lifecycle. The AAS can be understood as software entity providing asset's  information to  the  external by  means of a  standardized Application Programming Interface (API). In smart manufacturing, each physical thing or asset has its own administration shell, and each administration shell can connect with the other administration shell as shown in Figure 2.4 [29].
Figure 2. 4 Concept of Asset Administration Shell
Figure 2. 4 Concept of Asset Administration Shell

The structure of an AAS can be isolated into a digital factory (DF) header and body like shown in Figure  2.5 [11]. The concept of the DF  system has standardized in International Electrotechnical Commission (IEC) standard 62832 [10]. The DF header highlights a list of I4.0-compliant properties, such as identification of the physical asset and of the AAS [30]. This must be included to clearly assign the unique identity of the I4.0 Component. This property list is termed a manifest, characterized as 'an externally accessible defined set of meta-information, which provides information about the functional and non-functional properties of the I4.0 Component' [31]. The DF body contains a component manager that is mindfully responsible for the management of and access to services in individual submodels. Each submodel consists of hierarchically well-organized properties linked to various data or functions.

By using AAS, interoperability can be enhanced not only within company, but also between companies in the same supply chain network such as supplier and manufacturer. AAS also can be integrated with the other pillars in industry 4.0 such as Big Data since the data from the asset will be recorded over the lifecycle of asset (volume) for every second (veracity) and for every specification of asset (variety), Cloud Computing since the data will be stored and accessed from cloud, Simulation for doing trial and error based on scenario designed, and IoT that is embedded in assets.

AutomationML or Automation Markup Language or AML is pointed at accomplishing standardized and efficient data exchange during the engineering processes of a manufacturing system, which can reduce time and cost [12]. The main idea is, instead of developing a new data format for that  purpose, AutomationML adapts, extends, and merges already existing standardized data formats in an appropriate way. AML has been standardized in IEC 62714.

AML is an open and neutral XML-based data exchange format that can be utilized for product, process, and resource descriptions within the production-system engineering domain [32].  The  basic  structure  of  AutomationML  is  shown  in  Figure 2.6  [33].  The  core  of AutomationML is the top-level data format Computer Aided Engineering Exchange (CAEX), which connects distinctive engineering data formats, such as Collaborative Design Activity (COLLADA) and PLCopen XML [34]. Moreover, AutomationML has an inherent distributed architecture established on the concept of the object-oriented method, as does CAEX.

Open  Platform  Communications Unified  Architecture  (OPC UA) technology accomplishes message-based communication between clients and servers on different types of networks to  facilitate various leveled industrial  system  information exchange, such as  in connection to field devices, control systems, manufacturing execution systems, and enterprise resource planning systems [35]. OPC UA has been standardized in IEC 62541.

OPC UA follows client-server system. The OPC UA client uses the client application program interface (API) to send/receive OPC UA service request/response messages (Req/Rsp Msg) to/from the OPC UA server. Here, service is designed to discover the OPC UA servers that  are  available  in  a  particular  system  environment. Furthermore, the  client  API  was developed to act as an internal interface to set the client application code apart from the client communication stack. The role of the communication stack is to support data transportation between the client and server, which converts the client API calls to messages and sends them through the underlying communication entity to the OPC UA server [36]. In OPC UA Server, it has an 'address space' that is composed of sets of nodes, representing objects, variables, methods, and types of OPC UA metadata [12]. Figure 2.7 shows the OPC UA client/server architecture [37]. It figures the major elements of a typical OPC UA client and server as well as the communication process used to interact with each other.

In RAMI 4.0 perspective, OPC UA is located in the communication layer and serves as an interface for AAS communication. The advantage of OPC UA compared to Fieldbus and others is that OPC UA provides a unique information model composed of various node objects, properties, and references [10]. This is the reason why the AML model can be integrated into the OPC UA because the AML metadata can be mapped to the OPC UA nodes in a standardized manner [38].

Discrete-Event Simulation (DES) quantitatively represents the real world, simulates its dynamics on an event-by-event under uncertainty, and generates detailed performance report based on simulation. It  has become one of the mainstream computer-aided decision-making tools due to accessibility of effective computers [39]. Discrete event simulation (DES) is also a flexible modeling method characterized by the ability to represent complex behavior within, and interactions between individuals, populations, and their environments [40]. It can mimic operations that occur in a system with the help of advanced computer and software based on some assumptions so that the system can be studied scientifically [39].

In Digital  Twin  perspective, advanced simulation must be able to visualize the real system as similar as possible. With the help of advanced simulation software, now it can be achieved to use simulation as part of digital twin. Another thing that should be considered about simulation is it has a lot of advantages that support Industry 4.0 such as capability to do WhatIf analysis, simulation optimization, accurate report, and even showing dynamic dashboard.

Classical simulation usually used trial and error approach to find better solution. But it takes a lot of cost in perspective of time and less effective. Researchers have tried to integrate optimization technique such as metaheuristic to be embedded inside simulation software. One of famous algorithm that usually used in simulation optimization is Genetic Algorithm (GA) [41]. Based on this capability, it can achieve optimal decision in an efficient way.

Since simulation is one of the main technologies that support digital twin, determining simulation software should be  considered carefully based on  their  capability.  One  of the simulation software that provenly can be used as digital twin part is Flexsim software [42]. Flexsim is  developed and owned by Flexsim  Software Products, Inc. of Orem, Utah [43]. Flexsim  is  a  discrete-event, object-oriented simulator developed in  C++,  and using  Open Graphics Library (GL) technology. It has capability to animate the real system through tree view,  2-D, 3-D,  and virtual  reality.  Many  companies use Flexsim  to  improve production efficiencies and reduce operating costs through simulation, experimentation, and optimization [44].

There is  a lot  of simulation software that supports discrete-event system modeling. Compared with other simulation software, research from [45] gives the result that Flexsim is the best simulation software in 2018 and 2019 based on criteria Capability, General Purpose, Ease of Use, Popularity, and Development. Flexsim  has  so many features that  support digital  twin  concept. In  2017, Flexsim introduced new feature to  support physical-virtual interconnection called PLC  Emulation: Emulation tool to control 3D models with simulated programmable logic controllers (PLC) logic.  In  PLC  Emulation,  all  sensors  and  PLC  data  are  exchanged with  Open  Platform Communications (OPC) server or directly with PLC through serial communication protocol Modbus [42].

In  Flexsim, PLC  Emulation also can be combined with optimization feature called OptQuest  implementing  Evolutionary Algorithm  and  SQL  databases  access  that  makes FlexSim promising choice for prototyping and experimenting with digital twin concept. The illustration is shown in Figure 2.8 [42] where digital twin is implemented Shop-floor Service System  (SSS)  with  Shop-floor Digital  Twin  Data  (SDTD).  Flexsim  also  has  great  3D visualization and customizable dashboard so it will be easier to analyze the real system based on Flexsim-based virtual system.

The research about DT is done by [10] in realizing Plug-and-Produce for Industry 4.0. This research uses Asset Administration Shell framework to create DT between 3 Robots & 1 Turntable as physical assets and uses Web UI as static digital twin. To communicate between AAS, OPC UA & AML are used as main technologies. Sequence Diagram is also used to represent information flow between AAS. This research focuses on Adaptable Factories (AF) as industry 4.0 scenario to be developed. DT built has capability to control physical assets.

Different research [13] utilizes Operator to establish AAS with the help of Smart Jacket and create Human-Machine Interface (HMI) as static digital twin and it has capability to control physical assets. To communicate between AAS, OPC UA, NodeRED on MCU, and MQQT are  used as  main technologies. Block Diagram  is  also  used to  represent information flow between AAS. This research focuses on Operator Support in Production (OSP) as industry 4.0 scenario to be developed. Similar research focusing on the human as object of AAS is done by [46] that focuses on Operator Support in Production (OSP) as industry 4.0 scenario. Remote Control in Forklift Operator is used as physical asset. REST API and MQTT are used as main communication tool. GUI was created as static DT but it has no capability to control physical asset. Flowchart is used as information representation.

Some researchers also  have applied AAS  in  wider  area.  This  research [7]  utilizes assembly processes and create Human Machine Interface (HMI) as static digital twin and it has capability to control physical assets. OPC UA, CSV, JSON, and REST API are used as main technologies to communicate between AAS. This research focuses on Adaptable Factories (AF) as industry 4.0 scenario to be developed. The information flow between AAS is represent by a flowchart. Similar research focusing on DT application in assembly process is done by [47] especially in Plastic Production as physical assets and create 2D-based simulation as static digital twin and it has no capability to control physical assets. To communicate between AAS, MQTT & JSON are used as main technologies. Sequence diagram is also used to represent information flow between AAS. This research focuses on Smart Product Development for Smart Production (SP2) as industry 4.0 scenario to be developed. This research [48] uses robot station as physical assets to create digital twin. REST API, OPC UA, CSV, and JSON are used as communication tools between AAS. GUI is used as static DT and Flowchart is also used as information representation. This research focuses on Adaptable Factory (AF) as industry 4.0 scenario to be developed. DT created has capability to control the physical assets.

This research focuses on Operator Support in Production (SP2) as industry 4.0 scenario [14] that utilizes machine and operator and create Human-Machine Interface (HMI) as static digital twin. To communicate between AAS, JSON, and MQTT are used as main technologies. Block diagram is used to represent information flow between AAS. Similar research in SP2 [15] utilizes Air Quality Sensor and create Docker Image as static digital twin. To communicate between AAS, Kubernetes & Things Description (TD)/JSON are used as main technologies. Flowchart is also used to represent information flow between AAS.

This research [49] utilizes 2 robots & 2 conveyors and create Web-UI as static digital twin. To  communicate between AAS, OPC UA, and AML are used as main technologies. Sequence diagram is  also used to represent information flow between AAS. This research focuses on  Adaptable Factories  (AF)  as  industry  4.0  scenario to  be  developed. DT  has capability to control physical assets. Similar research also [11] utilizes a robot and create Flaskbased Web-UI as static digital twin. To communicate between AAS, ZeroMQ, RESTful, and HTTP are used as main technologies. ERD is also used to represent information flow between AAS. This research also focuses on Adaptable Factories (AF). Similar research [12] utilizes 2 robots & 2 conveyors and create Java-based GUI as static digital twin and it has capability to control physical assets. To communicate between AAS, OPC UA & AML are used as main technologies. Sequence diagram is also used to represent information flow between AAS. This research also focuses on Adaptable Factories (AF).

This research [37] utilizes 1 robot arm & 1 belt conveyor and create Human-Machine Interface (HMI) as static digital twin. To communicate between AAS, OPC UA & AML are used as  main technologies. Sequence diagram  is  also  used to  represent information flow between AAS. This research focuses on Adaptable Factories (AF) as industry 4.0 scenario to be developed. DT has capability to control physical assets. This research [50] utilizes 1 robot & 1 gripper. This research uses C++  based UI as digital twin and it has capability to control physical  assets.  To  communicate between  AAS,  OPC  UA  &  XML  are  used  as  main technologies. Class & sequence diagram is also used to represent information flow between AAS.  This  research focuses on  Adaptable Factories  (AF)  as  industry 4.0  scenario to  be developed. This research [51] focuses Adaptable Factory (AF) as industry 4.0 scenario. 1 motor and 1  drive are  used as physical assets. OPC  UA, NodeRED, and AML  are  used as main communication tool. Web UI was created as static DT and it has capability to control physical asset. Flowchart is used as information representation.

Another research focusing on Transparency and Adaptability of delivered Products (TAP) industry 4.0 scenario [52] utilizes Assembly Process & Thermosetting of Door Trims as  physical assets and create  Virtual  Reality  (VR)  as  dynamic digital  twin  and  it  has no capability to control physical assets. To communicate between AAS, RESTful API and XML are used as main technologies. Sequence diagram is also used to represent information flow between AAS. Similar research focusing on TAP is done by [53]. Industrial Valve is used as physical assets. FIWARE and AML are used used as main communication tool. Web UI was created as static DT and it has no capability to control physical asset. Use case diagram is used as information representation. Similar research on TAP also is done by [54] that utilizes Motor controller in assembly machine as physical asset. DT is not created so that it has no capability to control physical assets. To communicate between AAS, OPC UA and XML are developed as main technologies. Class diagram is used to represent information flow between AAS. This research also applied TAP as industry 4.0 scenario [55] that utilizes 1 motor & 1 drive. This research did not create anything related to digital twin. To communicate between AAS, REST API  &  JSON are  used as main  technologies. Sequence diagram is  also used to  represent information flow between AAS.

This research [56] focuses on SP2 as industry 4.0 scenario. Bulk container for energy system  is  used as  physical assets. REST  API,  HTTP,  and  JSON  are  used used  as  main communication tool. Docker image was created as static DT and it has capability to control physical asset. Sequence diagram is used as information representation. This research [57] focuses on  developing automatic predictive maintenance .  It  utilizes  Milling  machine as physical asset and create Azure UI as static digital twin and it has capability to control physical assets. To communicate between AAS, Zigbee was developed as main technologies. Use case diagram is used to represent information flow between AAS. This research focuses on Valuebased Service (VBS) as industry 4.0 scenario to be developed.

From 20 previous papers reviewed, the comparison is done with this research so that the novelty or contribution will be easily represented. State-of-the-art is shown in Table 2.3. by comparing some important criteria which are physical assets used, type of communication protocol and data  exchange, form of DT  created, information representation, Industry 4.0 scenario developed, control ability of DT, and optimization ability of DT.

State-of-the-art shows that previous studies about AAS application in realizing digital twin is very limited in visualization aspect which only shows static model rather than dynamic model. This  is  the  main drawback since  one of the  main functions of digital  twin  is  for enhancing monitoring. Besides that, they only considered a few specific assets and unmovable assets. However, practically there will  be  a  lot  of assets that  need to  be considered. This research uses 5 main asstes in warehouse including movable assets and propose submodels as well as communication network between them. This scenario in industry 4.0 is so-called Selforganizing Adaptive Logistics (SAL).  Most of the papers only focus on Adaptable Factory (AF)  for  the  purpose of  Plug-and-Produce. Moreover, there  is  still  no  publication about utilizing 3D-based simulation technology for realizing DT based on AAS framework especially using Flexsim software. Some previous studies also do not consider capability to control their assets from digital  twin. This is also drawback since it  only gives one flow communication rather than two flow communications. In fact, there is no single publication that enables DT for having optimization ability. Therefore, this research will propose a concept by providing dynamic digital twin for smart warehouse processes that provides optimization and controlling ability. This research will fulfill those gaps of digital twin development. By using simulation as dynamic model, a lot of advantages will be obtained and demonstrated. Altough this research does not reach implementation stage but this research differs from other studies and provide new concept for developing DT based on AAS framework.

elements.text: This research will follow 4 main stages. First, AAS variables definition is done starting from identifying the assets and the data that want to be exchanged via AAS including the IoT devices, as  well  as  defining AAS  capability and AAS  structure. Second, AAS  simulation modeling with  Flexsim software is  established. Third,  AAS  system integration. And  last, demonstrating some  main  advantages of  using  simulation model  as  part  of  digital  twin. Research flowchart is shown in Figure 3.1 and the detailed information is described below.

AAS Variables Definition stage defines the assets that want to be created administration shell for. Smart warehouse is chosen as research object. By using smart warehouse, some new assets will be considered. Since previous studies only considered specific assets and unmovable assets such as arm robots, conveyors, etc., thus this research will consider more comprehensive main assets available in  Smart Warehouse. One of smart warehouse in Taipei is  observed directly to identify main assets in smart warehouse operation.

After all assets have been identified, AAS capabilities are designed. It determines what data will be collected and what feedback will be given, including IoT devices that will be used. To  define the  structure  of  AAS  for  each  assets,  AAS  template  proposed by  [49]  gives comprehensive scope like shown in Figure 3.2. This research will use that template since it is defined AAS structure from DF Header to DF Body and will ease to identify submodels of AAS. Since this research does not reach implementation stage, not all submodels are applied such as documentation in generic submodel.

This research will  propose simulation model as part of dynamic digital  twin. Since warehouse process can be  represented with  discrete-event simulation, Flexsim  simulation software is chosen. In digital twin, not only functional is important but also visual is crucial. Flexsim uses three-dimensional (3D) visualization that can imitate operations very similar. In this  research, Flexsim 2021 version is  used. Not  all  versions can be  used for digital  twin purposes because of communication limitations especially for Flexsim under 2020 version, it does not support OPC UA but supports OPC Data Access (DA) and Modbus protocol.

In digital twin modeling, simulation modeling approach will be different compared with classical simulation modeling. It should not be valid but must be verified structurally and by definition. In the other words, it should not imitate the behavior perfectly but must imitate the structure of system. Because later on, it will be connected with physical assets in real-time.

Simulation modeling will  follow 5  main stages.  First,  conceptual modeling. It  will produce flowchart related to process sequence of smart warehouse operations. Second, layout design of smart warehouse. Third, creating some objects/assets needed. This should be the same as AAS variables defined before. Fourth, defining the logic of each asset. Two approaches are used in modeling which are standard object modeling to define general behavior of assets and process flow to imitate the specific behavior. The last will be verifying process. The logic of simulation must be similar to conceptual model and must be no error.

AAS System Integration consists of designing communication system network based on AAS framework and Information modeling. AAS framework will develop how assets can communicate with other AASs and what communication devices will be used. On the other side, information modeling will be represented by sequence diagram to show how control flow and data flow in AAS  system. It is  created based on RAMI  4.0 layers. The communication protocol and data exchange type will be determined based on the relevance and compliance with simulation software used and convention in industry 4.0 community.

Since  this  research  proposes simulation  as  digital  twin  especially  using  Flexsim software, the  demonstrations are  needed to  show  the  main  advantages of  using  Flexsim software in digital twin system. Two demonstrations will be shown which are simulation-based optimization and creating dynamic dashboard.

In classical simulation, What-If analysis usually are used to get better decision. But it is less  effective  in  decision  making  so  that  nowadays optimization is  integrated  with  simulation. However, if the real condition is too dynamic, the decision needs to be taken fast and what-if analysis is more appropriate used rather than optimization. The process of simulation-based optimization in this research will follow iterative model [58]. Metaheuristic algorithm will give input parameters and simulation will use them to be simulated. Then the results will be given back to the algorithm. After that, metaheuristic algorithm will improve it and produce new input parameters. The process will be iterated until the number of iterations reached.

Metaheurisitic algorithm used in this research is Genetic Algorithm (GA) by following OptQuest optimizer [59]. The process of classical GA can be seen in Figure 3.3 [60]. Since optimizer is embedded in Flexsim, all parameters such as population size, crossover rate, and mutation rate have been fixed. There is no elitism strategy used in this original GA.

The scenario of simulation-based optimization in this research will be AGV capacity planning. The idea behind it is how many goods should be brought for each AGV so that it will maximize throughput and minimize energy usage simultaneously under uncertain conditions. Since the problem does not have an analytical closed-form so that it cannot be solved with classical  optimization technique or  mathematical programming  such as  calculus or  linear programming, then simulation is the one to calculate objective functions under uncertainties.

The trade-off in this AGV capacity planning problem is the more goods brought in one delivery, the  more energy  usage  needed for AGV  due to  the  more weight  and the  more loading/unloading time needed. Since there are 2 objectives, then multi-objective optimization is done by using Pareto Optimality approach. This approach will give a set of optimal solutions based on Non-dominated Sorting Genetic Algorithm II (NSGA-II) and users can choose based on their preferences. To select the single solution, Weighted Sum Method also will be used. The framework of simulation-based optimization for AGV Capacity Planning is  shown in Figure 3.4.

Since the objectives have different unit (throughput is in unit and energy usage is in amp), therefore normalization is needed first before weighted sum method is applied to choose the best solution. Normalization is done by using min-max method to unify the scale for each objective. The equation of normalization is shown in Equation 1. For weighted sum method equation is shown in Equation 2. Where x = decision variables, w = weight, f(x) = objective function.

The second demonstration is creating dynamic dashboard. One of the main advantages of using simulation software is the accuracy of calculating performance parameters for each object in system. It can be recorded and performed via dashboard in real-time. This supports digital twin purpose which can ease monitoring and controlling process. Some parameters that are created in  the dashboard are AGVs utilization (%), Total  Throughput for each type of product (Unit), Forklift State (%), and Operator State (%). However, these parameters can be customized later on based on user preferences.

In  this  chapter, the  implementation and discussion will  be  presented based on the sequence of research methods. First, the assets considered in smart warehouse will be discussed including main assets and supporting assets as well as the results of defining the AAS based on its capability and structure. Second, the simulation model result will be presented. Third, the result of system integration analysis will be shown in order to achieve bi-directional connection between physical assets and digital assets. Last, simulation-based optimization and dynamic dashboard results will be discussed.

Smart  warehouse has a  lot  of  assets to  support smart warehouse business process. Through direct observation and interview, there are 5 main assets that will be considered in AAS  framework namely AGV, Operator, Conveyor, Forklift,  and  Storage Rack (Pod).  To record the data from these assets and give feedback to these assets, some sensors and controllers are also needed as supporting assets as shown in Figure 4.1. Direct arrows from supporting asset to  main asset describe the  relation and the  usage of controller/sensor with the asset. Simulation User Interface (UI) is basically Flexsim software as digital model.

Sensing capability and controlling capability between digital asset and physical asset are explained in AAS  Capability as shown in Table 4.1. Since this research uses packaged simulation software, not all  assets have capability to be controlled because of limitation of software. This  is  the  main  reason why  previous study created  HMI/GUI  to  enhance the flexibility of control. However, the main capabilities still can be captured. Integration between HMI/GUI also can be made with packaged software to increase efficiency and flexibility.

elements.text: AGV will send position data, speed data, and capacity data to digital twin. Position data will be in the form of coordinate (x, y) so that digital twin can capture the movement of AGV and can be visualized in real-time. This concept also will be applied to Forklift and Operator asset which are movable assets. For Operator, position data can be achieved by advanced tag embedded in smart jacket that will  be  used by operator. Speed data will  record the speed movement of AGV with meter/second unit, this should be equal to digital model. Capacity data depend on what the steering control  system program is.  Capacity data reflect  how  many packages or goods that can be brought per delivery for AGV. This steering control system also has other controls for AGV like route and picking strategy. For controlling capability, it shows that digital twin should be able to control the speed and capacity of AGV. This is suitable with Flexsim software capability to control physical assets.

Conveyor will have another sensor in addition to speed sensor which is delivery path based on Semantic Product Memory (SemProM). Since warehouse will have some types of products, SemProM concept will be adopted to differ product types and object detector will recognize it. Object detector will be applied in every intersection of conveyor. This information is very important because digital twin needs to recognize which path in conveyor that each product type will go. This concept also will be applied in Cell-based Position storage rack since digital twin needs to recognize in which cell that a product type comes in and out. Object detector will be applied in each cell of rack and when product enters, data are sent to digital model. This  concept also should be applied in every starting point and ending point of the process so that digital model can recognize product that come in and come out.

After define AAS capability, AAS for each asset needs to be defined based on AAS structure. Later on, this structure will be applied in Automation Markup Language (AML) when the implementation stage is carried on. In this research, AAS template proposed by [49] is used. The result of AAS definition is shown in Table 4. 2. The structure of an AAS can be divided into a Digital Factory (DF) header and a DF body based on the concept of the DF framework benchmarked in International Electrotechnical Commission (IEC)  standard 62832 [9].  DF header describes a list  of I4.0-compliant properties or usually called manifest and DF body contains a component manager.

DF header consists of asset identifier (Asset ID) to differ each type of asset, AAS ID to differ every AAS even in the same asset family, for example AGV 1 and AGV 2 will  have different AAS ID even though they are the same asset, Number of Generic Submodels, and Number of Asset-Specific Submodels. Every ID must be unique to ensure that the information in  submodels can be located appropriately and communicated between AAS in a  common semantic manner so that interoperability can be realized.

Generic submodel in DF body means basic standardized submodel applicable to a broad variety  of  assets.  Every  AAS  must  include  generic  submodels  to  represent  mandatory information on assets. Index Data Item (IDI) submodel is the entry point of all of the other submodels which means that it is essentially a table of contents enabling efficient searching of all submodels. Property Value Statement (PVS) submodel contains metadata that allows users to discover the attributes of the asset such as names, versions, and also documentation. Some of  these  properties may  change along the  asset  lifecycle.  Hence, this  submodel must  be upgraded regularly. Communication (CM) submodel stores information about communication capabilities or communication protocol of the asset.

When  generic  submodel  informs  static  data,  contrarily  Asset-Specific  submodel informs dynamic data containing specific information about asset functions. Different assets require different submodels to reflect specialized functions. In this manner, considering the variety and complexity of each asset function, the number of asset-specific submodels differs. For  example, AGVs have speed submodel with real  value but operators do not  have this submodel. Operators will have position submodel with real value because digital model does not need to sense the speed of operators but needs to sense the position of operators. This determination depends on how the physical assets want to be reflected in digital twin.

Digital  twin  should be  started  by  detailed  simulation  modeling.  Without  a  good simulation model, digital twin will not reflect physical system well. Before simulation model is created, the conceptual model of smart warehouse process should be clearly described first as  shown in  Figure  4. 2.  Layout design is  shown in  Figure  4. 3.  The flow of warehouse operations will be described as follows. When goods are arrived by truck, arrival goods will be received by forklift and goods will be sent to the Quality Control (QC) process. QC process will not generate waste products but it only checks the number and quality of products. Then, storage planning will  be done to  determine whether the goods will  be stored in  long-term storage or short-term storage. Short-term storage only stores the goods that will be sent in the same day, conversely long-term storage only stores the goods that will be sent in another day. After storage planning has been determined, Putaway process will be done by forklift either it comes from QC process to short-term storage or from long-term storage to short-term storage. When the pick-up time arrives, Order picking process is done by AGVs. AGVs will pick goods directly in short-term storage in their trajectory. The goods will be sent to shipping stage that consists of sorting and packaging process. Work in Process (WIP) from sorting process will be stored in the rack temporarily if the packaging process is not finished yet.

However, this research will demonstrate some advantages of simulation as part of digital twin so that input data such as processing time and capacity will be assumed based on statistical distribution to capture uncertainty. Input data are shown in Table 4. 3. The result of simulation model is shown in Figure 4. 4 and Figure 4. 5. This simulation model also has been verified which are following the logic of conceptual model and no error recognized such as deadlock or even collision between AGV.

The proposed concept that wants to be achieved in this research is basically system integration to integrate industry 4.0 technologies such as IoT, Simulation, Cloud Computing, Big Data Analytics, and others with emphasizing of digital twin like shown in Figure 4.6. In brief description, data from smart  warehouse will  be recorded by IoT  and will  be sent to simulation model as  digital  twin  through cloud in  real-time. Later  on, simulation can  be extended to be Augmented Reality (AR) or Virtual Reality (VR). From simulation, command or control strategy can be sent to smart warehouse through cloud as well. Transmitted data can be stored as big data in the cloud to apply data analytics so that it can enhance warehousing process through Machine Learning (ML), Deep Learning (DL), or Artificial Intelligence (AI).
Figure 4. 6 Proposed Concept Development through Digital Twin System
Figure 4. 6 Proposed Concept Development through Digital Twin System

Related to data sensing from assets especially for position data, it will be sensed from a transmitter on the top and it  will  record the  tag  embedded in movable assets so  that the movement can be recognized in digital twin as shown in Figure 4. 7. It  can be achieved by some approaches that already exist nowadays such as Wi-Fi positioning system, RFID longrange, etc. These data will  correspond with Flexsim in  position property so that  they will connect in real-time. For SemProM in storage rack, in order to recognize which cell in rack that each product will go, it will  correspond with object detector embedded in every cell as shown in Figure 4. 8. These data will correspond with Flexsim in rack property which is level (row) or bay (column) so that they can connect in real-time. For SemProM in conveyor, to recognize which path in conveyor that each product will go,  it will  correspond with object detector embedded in every intersection of conveyor like shown in Figure 4. 9. These data will correspond with Flexsim in decision point property so that they can connect in real-time.

Digital  twin should not only enable one-direction flow from physical to digital asset (data flow), but it also should enable bi-direction flow from digital to physical asset (control flow). This research allows digital twin to control speed of AGV, capacity of AGV, and speed of conveyor as shown in Figure 4. 10. In addition, the most important point is the requirement part for simulation software. It should be fulfilled especially for connectivity issues. Flexsim allows OPC UA connection based on emulation tool so that control flow can be done and new parameters can be applied with simulated programmable logic controllers (PLC).

There are two modes in the emulation tool to  make a change which are Active and Inactive. Direct change should be checked as Active to make a change in real-time. This feature allows users to control physical assets directly from digital twin. Otherwise, it will not make a change if direct change mode is Inactive. Inactive mode option can be used whenever trial & error analysis or optimization is needed. After optimum parameter is  known, then it  can be applied with Active mode. It is worth noting that not all Flexsim versions can be used for digital twin purposes because of communication limitations especially for Flexsim under 2020 version that does not support OPC UA communication but it supports OPC DA and Modbus protocol. The configuration of sensors and controls also should be clearly defined in Flexsim based on AAS Capability as shown in Figure 4. 11. Later on, if implementation stage should be done, Tag ID must be corresponded with the ID of related AAS and associated with object in Flexsim.
Figure 4. 10 AAS Correspondence for Controllable Part
Figure 4. 10 AAS Correspondence for Controllable Part
Figure 4. 11 Configuration of Sensors and Controls in AAS Flexsim
Figure 4. 11 Configuration of Sensors and Controls in AAS Flexsim

AAS needs system communication network to implement digital twin. Therefore, AAS network structure for a smart warehouse including the assets and data exchange paths is shown in Figure 4. 12. As stated before, in this research OPC UA and AML are used as main backbone communication between AAS. In simple words, AML will answer what data will be exchanged and OPC UA will answer how data are communicated.

There are 3 reasons why OPC UA and AML are chosen. First, OPC UA has been standardized in IEC 62541 and AML has been standardized in IEC 62714. Second, they are compatible with Flexsim software as digital model. Third, AML and OPC UA adhere to the I4.0 conventions and comply with the RAMI 4.0 model. In AAS system, each asset has a unique AAS ID. However, in terms of simplicity for representation, there are several numbers of the same assets like there are 5 AGVs in smart warehouse but it will only show one AGV in Figure 4. 12 because it will have similar AAS with other AGVs but different ID. This figure shows how AAS connects each other and what communication they use.
Figure 4. 12 AAS Framework for Smart Warehouse
Figure 4. 12 AAS Framework for Smart Warehouse

Take a  look  at  AGV  subsystem, there  will  be  speed sensor  and  speed controller connected with AGV through Universal Asynchronous Receiver-Transmitter (UART). There is also  position  sensor  to  sense  the  position  of  AGV  connected  through  radio  waves.  AGV  itself will be connected with Steering Control System through WiFi.  Steering Control System has capability to control speed, picking strategy such as AGV capacity, and route.

Steering Control System will be connected with Gateway through OPC UA. There are some gateways that can be used. One of them is LM Gateway201-OPC UA protocol. It supports wired and wireless protocols. The gateway has two functions which are data storage in AML and data exchange via OPC UA. From the gateway, it  will  connect with AAS of Flexsim through OPC UA and Flexsim will show real-time condition through external interface.

The interaction between AAS is  shown as a sequence diagram in Figure  4. 13 that represents the dynamic information flow and control flow across the digitalized network of AASs by following RAMI 4.0 layers. First, the AML-related OPC UA server will be initialized. Then, OPC UA sessions will be created with different clients which are OPC UA Client from AAS of Flexsim and OPC UA Interface from AAS of Field devices. Control flows are then generated by the users from AAS Flexsim and passed down to the AASs of the field devices. Here, warehousing tasks are executed according to the control strategy. Feedback parameters are then given back to the AAS of Flexsim. Thus, the digital twin system operates in a loop.

Two main advantages of simulation will  be demonstrated in this research which are simulation-based optimization and dynamic dashboard. All of these features are embedded in the software so that it will be practically easy to use by the users. This optimizer solves a gap from previous state-of-the-art analysis about DT that even tough previous researches about DT were done, but there are still lack of DT that can reflect optimization [16].

elements.section_title: 4.4.1 Simulation-based Optimization for AGV Capacity Planning
elements.text: AGV takes crucial part in smart warehouse operation. It brings goods from storage to the shipping area and it has their own trajectory. Capacity of AGV determines total throughput and energy usage since AGV uses electricity energy in their operation. However, the more goods carried out, the heavier they are that takes longer loading & unloading time and the more energy usage needed. Therefore, there is trade-off in this problem. Even tough there are some objectives also that can be considered such as optimizing the route of AGV and the utilization of worker in warehouse, but only total throughput and energy usage will  be considered here since those objectives influence the customer satisfaction, profit, and operation cost directly.

elements.section_title: 4.4.1 Simulation-based Optimization for AGV Capacity Planning
elements.text: To  solve  Multi-Objective  Optimization  (MOO),  GA  based  on  NSGA-II  is  used. Simulation brings more advanced optimization by considering uncertain conditions such as goods availability and process time. Simulation is run for 1 day operation or 7 hours or 25200 seconds working time. It is  assumed that every load of goods brought by AGV will take 2 ampere per meter and if there are no goods brought it will only take 1 ampere per meter. There is also no charging condition considered. The optimization code used is shown in Figure 14. The results for GA searching within 100 iterations are shown in Figure 4. 15 for throughput (unit) and Figure 4. 16 for energy consumption in ampere (amp). The purple circle shows the suggested candidate solution. The set of non-dominated solutions is shown in Table 4. 4.
Figure 4. 15 Optimization Result for Maximizing Throughput
Figure 4. 15 Optimization Result for Maximizing Throughput
Figure 4. 16 Optimization Result for Minimizing Energy Usage
Figure 4. 16 Optimization Result for Minimizing Energy Usage
Table 4. 4 Non-Dominated Solutions through Pareto Optimality

Since pareto optimality gives a set of optimal solutions, the users can choose which the best option that they want based on their preferences. From this result, it is known that even if AGVs use maximum capacity (25) to bring goods, it  does not give optimal result. It gives higher energy usage because AGVs need to travel back & forth with too much load that affect energy needed. However, the throughput is not good enough because bringing more goods will give longer loading and unloading time. It is also because the availability of goods is not always ready because of uncertainty from previous process.

If it  is  calculated by using  Weighted Sum  Method by giving  more weight  to total throughput (0.6) and another (0.4) for energy consumption criterion, it gives solution ID 95 as the most  optimum solution like  shown in  Table 4.  5. Hence, the  optimum capacity under uncertainty for each AGV is AGV 1 (X1) = 9, AGV 2 (X2) = 9, AGV 3 (X3) = 9, AGV 4 (X4) = 8, AGV 5 (X5) = 9.

It cannot be denied that monitoring and controlling is the key to make good decisions in operation. This is  the main purpose of industry 4.0 as well that can be achieved through digital twin technology. Therefore, the dashboard is one of the tools that can be used. This is useful  to  detect  problems  with  visualization  rather  than  numbers.  Through  simulation technology, the dashboard can be very accurate and real-time as well. Hence, dashboard for smart warehouse is created by using Flexsim simulation software feature for some important parameters such as total throughput, Forklift State, Operator State, and AGV Utilization. The dashboard while simulation running is shown in Figure 4. 17.

Total throughput will inform users about how many packaged goods for each type of product are ready to be delivered. Forklift State and Operator State will inform users about the state  percentage of forklifts and operators like  how long  they are  idle  and utilized. AGV Utilization informs users about how long AGV bringin goods or bringing empty and loading or  unloading. Dashboard will be  updated in real-time. It  will  benefit from the monitoring aspect. These data can be customized based on user preferences as well. Later on, data from dashboard also can be exported to database and predictive analytics can be done.

Related to optimization purpose, Figure 4.18 and Figure 4.19 show dashboard before and after optimization. Even though optimized result decreases total throughput as 1.62% but it can save AGV energy usage as 8.4%. It can save operational cost and extend AGV's life cycle as well. From AGV utilization, optimized result also gives higher percentage of traveling but lower percentage of loading/unloading. However longer traveling does not mean higher energy usage, but it depends also with how many loads that AGV brings per travel. By using this kind of flexible dashboard, it will ease users to take decision in order to optimize warehouse operation under uncertainty based on simulation-based digital twin. The more interesting one is, this proposed concept can implement the optimum decision directly from the software to the shopfloor without changing it from shopfloor manually. The configuration of this control application is shown in Figure 4. 20.

The new concept of simulation-based digital twin based on Asset Administration Shell (AAS) framework has been proposed by using Flexsim software with smart warehouse as a use-case. Asset-specific submodels also have been proposed for Automated Guided Vehicle (AGV),  Operator,  Conveyor, Forklift,  and  Storage  Rack.  AAS  capability  also  has  been designed which digital twin is able to monitor and control the real system as well as providing optimization. It  needs OPC  UA  and AutomationML as  communication protocol and data exchange type between AAS.

The verified simulation model imitating smart warehouse has been constructed as well built in Flexsim software. It has imitated the main assets in smart warehouse as well as the layout and logic behind it. System integration architecture also has been proposed through AAS framework and sequence diagram to help the understanding on how data and control flow from all AASs including AAS of Flexsim as digital twin.

Since this research proposes simulation with Flexsim software as digital twin, two main advantages have been demonstrated. The result of simulation-based optimization for multiobjective AGV capacity planning shows that in order to maximize the total throughput and minimize energy usage simultaneously, solution ID 95 gives optimum result where the capacity for each AGV is as follows: AGV 1 (X1) = 9, AGV 2 (X2) = 9, AGV 3 (X3) = 9, AGV 4 (X4) = 8, AGV 5 (X5) = 9. This is going to be breakthrough for Digital Twin research since previous state-of-the-art analysis about DT stated that even there are still  lack of DT that can reflect optimization. The  result  of designing  dynamic dashboard  also has  been demonstrated to increase the capability and accuracy of controlling and monitoring such as total throughput for each product type, AGV Utilization, and Operator State.
Recommendation will be given for two stakeholders, namely smart warehouse and further work as follows:

Smart  warehouse has not only a lot  of assets but also movable assets that need to be analyzed carefully. This is because warehouse is an important entity in logistics. In order to enhance  smart warehouse  operation,  system  integration through  digital twin establishment based on  AAS  framework is  very appropriate to  be  implemented, this research is a starting point to implement digital twin as the basic technology for system integration. Two-stage DT application has been done in this research which are system design of AAS and simulation modeling. Other warehouses also can use this proposed concept as well  as methodology for establishing simulation-based digital twin that  has been constructed in this  research and start  to  apply 2 next stages  which are  hardware installation and PLC programming to connect digital assets and physical assets based on the proposed communication protocol.

In  reality, there are still  many lacks  of industry 4.0 scenario application especially in system integration. Moreover, there is still a few researches working on AAS as the key of integration and standardization. Since this research contributes in proposing simulation model especially Flexsim  software as dynamic digital twin  and have tried to  consider assets a wider area, further work can start to research in the implementation stage and find efficient way. Economic analysis also should be considered in order to achieve minimum cost in implementing digital twin. Until today, it is still hard to establish standard manner to deploy digital  twin without AAS.  Later on, a lot of industries cannot be integrated. Without standardization, each industry will have its own digital twin and each industry will stand by itself without any integration and communication between them. That is not what industry 4.0 targeted. Moreover, this proposed concept also can be integrated with data analytics by using the same AAS framework with some additional submodels. Some of data will be sent to the simulation that will be used as monitoring and controlling based on optimized decision and others will  be  stored in  the cloud as  big  data to  establish predictive maintenance and give the control to the physical asset automatically. Digital twin from simulation also can be extended into AR or VR to enhance its capability. Thus, industry 4.0 scenarios can be integrated systematically and comprehensively.

The need for improving flexibility, optimality, and transparency of industry processes increases since the  customer demands are highly  diverse and full of uncertainty. CyberPhysical System (CPS) technology now is being developed to meet those requirements. It can be achieved through Digital Twin (DT). Unfortunately, the application of DT is still limited in practice nowadays, and no standard way to achieve integration. The concept of an Asset Administration Shell (AAS) proposed by Plattform Industrie 4.0 arose as a promising concept to realize DT in standard manner. However, the granularity of AAS remains undefined and still  under development. A literature study shows that most of studies only reached static digital twin and only considered a few specific assets especially unmovable assets. Dynamic digital twin is only supported by Virtual Reality (VR) that cannot be used for optimization as well as direct controlling. Therefore, this research intends to contribute to DT development by  proposing 3D  computer simulation technology as  dynamic digital  twin  by  following Reference Architecture Model Industrie 4.0 (RAMI  4.0) based on AAS

Framework. The proposed concept enables DT to do dynamic monitoring, optimization, and direct controlling. As a use case, a smart warehouse in Taiwan is used and assets considered include Automated Guided Vehicles (AGVs), Operator, Conveyor, Forklift, and Storage Rack. This research consists of 4 stages. First, AAS Variables Definition, identifying the assets and the data that want to be exchanged via AAS, defining AAS capability and AAS structure. Second, AAS Simulation Modeling with Flexsim software is established. Third, AAS System Integration consists  of  designing  communication  networks  and  information  modeling.  And  last, demonstrating  2  main  advantages  of  using  simulation  which  are simulation-based optimization  for  AGV  capacity  planning  and  creating  dynamic  dashboard. To  support communication between assets,  OPC  Unified Architecture  (OPC  UA)  and  Automation Markup  Language  (AutomationML)  are  determined.  As  a  result  of  demonstration, simulation-based optimization is done for multi-objectives and can find the optimum capacity of each AGV. Dynamic dashboard is also created to ease real-time monitoring process. Later on, data from dashboard can be exported to database and predictive analytics can be done. Based on these  capabilities, industry 4.0 scenarios can be  integrated  systematically and comprehensively.
Keywords : Asset Administration Shell, Digital Twin, Simulation, Optimization

In discussing Industry 4.0, there is a framework that approaches the issue of Industry 4.0 in a structured manner, namely Reference Architecture Model for Industry 4.0 (RAMI 4.0) proposed by German Plattform Industrie 4.0 shown in Figure 2.1 [5]. Actually, there are also other frameworks with the same purpose like Industrial Internet Reference Architecture (IIRA) proposed by IIC from US  [20], IBM  Industry 4.0 Architecture proposed by IBM [21], and NIST Smart Manufacturing [22].
Compared to others,  RAMI  4.0  gives  more comprehensive information and  more relevant to be implemented in industry especially for smart manufacturing [21]. RAMI 4.0 provides an orientation for plotting the requirements of sectors together with standards in order to define and further develop Industry 4.0 [23]. It is implemented in Industry 4.0 aspects for smart manufacturing which combines all elements and IT components [24].

Since the main challenge of industry 4.0 is interoperability, it is also shown in RAMI 4.0 from architectural layers which are divided into 2 aspects, namely physical aspects and digital  aspects. The  physical thing  is  called an  asset, while  the  digital  aspect  starts  from communication layers until business layers as shown in Figure 2.1. To change the physical thing  to the digital,  there is  integration layer between asset and communication layers that applies the Digital Twin (DT) concept.
Figure 2. 1 Reference Architecture Model for Industry 4.0

<!-- image -->
(Source: [5])

The concept of the Digital  Twin (DT)  came from the presentation in 2002 entitled 'Conceptual Ideal for Product Lifecycle Management (PLM)' by Dr. Grieves [25]. It is called 'Twin' because it is like mirroring or twinning of systems between what existed in real space to what existed in virtual space and vice versa. But at that time, internet was still expensive and limited. Since DT uses internet as the basic technology so that the development of DT did not appear. But  today, internet becomes cheaper and borderless so  that  many industries have implemented DT to enhance interoperability across value stream of an asset like  shown in Figure 2.2 [26].
The concept of DT will be different with the other modeling concept even others show like mirroring the physical system. For example, Computer Aided Manufacturing (CAM) is also mirroring the physical system but it does not have capability to connect physical system with digital  system with bi-directional. This is the main difference of DT concept compared with others. In DT, digital system will be connected in real-time and have capability to control physical system. However, CAM or others concept can also be applied as part of DT.

<!-- image -->
(Source: [26])
Digital twin (DT) is known as the basic concept to support integration in Industry 4.0 and refers to virtual models of an asset that are fully integrated with a real thing/asset [27].  In DT, digital asset and physical asset are connected by internet with semantic relationships. It can be used for virtual testing, analyzing collected data, and predicting future behavior of physical things before applying it to real things [15]. Since DT has so many advantages, DT can be practically applied in almost every industry like shown in Table 2.1.
Table 2. 1 Digital Twin in Practice
(Source:[28])
<!-- image -->

Besides that, DT also can solve information silos problems as shown in Figure  2.3. Traditionally, the information about an asset is usually scattered across multiple information sources,  which  are  maintained  by  different  organizations.  It will  result  in  du plicated, inconsistent, and missing information. With digital twin, it can collect data centrally for every entity and then makes that information available to different areas of the business for their specific  applications  through  integration  interfaces,  such  as  Application  Programming Interfaces (APIs) [29]. This improves decision-making through a shared understanding and reduces the overall lifecycle cost of operating and maintaining a plant.
<!-- image -->
· VR, AR models
Figure 2. 3 Digital Twin to Solve Information Silos Problem
(Source: [29])

One of the approaches to realize Digital Twin in manufacturing industry is called Asset Administration Shell (AAS) [29]. AAS basically consists of two terms which are 'Asset' and 'Administration Shell'.  The  asset  refers  to  the  physical  things  e.g.  machine, product, & materials, and the administration shell refers to the digital thing that stores information about the asset over its  entire lifecycle. The AAS can be understood as software entity providing asset's  information to  the  external by  means of a  standardized Application Programming Interface (API). In smart manufacturing, each physical thing or asset has its own administration shell, and each administration shell can connect with the other administration shell as shown in Figure 2.4 [29].
Figure 2. 4 Concept of Asset Administration Shell

<!-- image -->
(Source: [29])

The structure of an AAS can be isolated into a digital factory (DF) header and body like shown in Figure  2.5 [11]. The concept of the DF  system has standardized in International Electrotechnical Commission (IEC) standard 62832 [10]. The DF header highlights a list of I4.0-compliant properties, such as identification of the physical asset and of the AAS [30]. This must be included to clearly assign the unique identity of the I4.0 Component. This property list is termed a manifest, characterized as 'an externally accessible defined set of meta-information, which provides information about the functional and non-functional properties of the I4.0 Component' [31]. AutomationML or Automation Markup Language or AML is pointed at accomplishing standardized and efficient data exchange during the engineering processes of a manufacturing system, which can reduce time and cost [12]. The main idea is, instead of developing a new data format for that  purpose, AutomationML adapts, extends, and merges already existing standardized data formats in an appropriate way. AML has been standardized in IEC 62714.
AML is an open and neutral XML-based data exchange format that can be utilized for product, process, and resource descriptions within the production-system engineering domain [32]. The  core  of AutomationML is the top-level data format Computer Aided Engineering Exchange (CAEX), which connects distinctive engineering data formats, such as Collaborative Design Activity (COLLADA) and PLCopen XML [34]. Moreover, AutomationML has an inherent distributed architecture established on the concept of the object-oriented method, as does CAEX.

Open  Platform  Communications Unified  Architecture  (OPC UA) technology accomplishes message-based communication between clients and servers on different types of networks to  facilitate various leveled industrial  system  information exchange, such as  in connection to field devices, control systems, manufacturing execution systems, and enterprise resource planning systems [35]. OPC UA has been standardized in IEC 62541.

OPC UA follows client-server system. The OPC UA client uses the client application program interface (API) to send/receive OPC UA service request/response messages (Req/Rsp Msg) to/from the OPC UA server. Here, service is designed to discover the OPC UA servers that  are  available  in  a  particular  system  environment. Furthermore, the  client  API  was developed to act as an internal interface to set the client application code apart from the client communication stack. The role of the communication stack is to support data transportation between the client and server, which converts the client API calls to messages and sends them through the underlying communication entity to the OPC UA server [36]. In OPC UA Server, it has an 'address space' that is composed of sets of nodes, representing objects, variables, methods, and types of OPC UA metadata [12]. Figure 2.7 shows the OPC UA client/server architecture [37]. It figures the major elements of a typical OPC UA client and server as well as the communication process used to interact with each other.

Discrete-Event Simulation (DES) quantitatively represents the real world, simulates its dynamics on an event-by-event under uncertainty, and generates detailed performance report based on simulation. It  has become one of the mainstream computer-aided decision-making tools due to accessibility of effective computers [39]. Discrete event simulation (DES) is also a flexible modeling method characterized by the ability to represent complex behavior within, and interactions between individuals, populations, and their environments [40]. It can mimic operations that occur in a system with the help of advanced computer and software based on some assumptions so that the system can be studied scientifically [39].
In Digital  Twin  perspective, advanced simulation must be able to visualize the real system as similar as possible. With the help of advanced simulation software, now it can be achieved to use simulation as part of digital twin. Another thing that should be considered about simulation is it has a lot of advantages that support Industry 4.0 such as capability to do WhatIf analysis, simulation optimization, accurate report, and even showing dynamic dashboard.

Classical simulation usually used trial and error approach to find better solution. But it takes a lot of cost in perspective of time and less effective. Researchers have tried to integrate optimization technique such as metaheuristic to be embedded inside simulation software. One of famous algorithm that usually used in simulation optimization is Genetic Algorithm (GA) [41]. Based on this capability, it can achieve optimal decision in an efficient way.

This research will  propose simulation model as part of dynamic digital  twin. Since warehouse process can be  represented with  discrete-event simulation, Flexsim  simulation software is chosen. In digital twin, not only functional is important but also visual is crucial. Flexsim uses three-dimensional (3D) visualization that can imitate operations very similar. Not  all  versions can be  used for digital  twin purposes because of communication limitations especially for Flexsim under 2020 version, it does not support OPC UA but supports OPC Data Access (DA) and Modbus protocol.
In digital twin modeling, simulation modeling approach will be different compared with classical simulation modeling. It should not be valid but must be verified structurally and by definition. In the other words, it should not imitate the behavior perfectly but must imitate the structure of system. Because later on, it will be connected with physical assets in real-time.

Simulation modeling will  follow 5  main stages.  First,  conceptual modeling. It  will produce flowchart related to process sequence of smart warehouse operations. Second, layout design of smart warehouse. Third, creating some objects/assets needed. This should be the same as AAS variables defined before. Fourth, defining the logic of each asset. Two approaches are used in modeling which are standard object modeling to define general behavior of assets and process flow to imitate the specific behavior. The last will be verifying process. The logic of simulation must be similar to conceptual model and must be no error.

AAS System Integration consists of designing communication system network based on AAS framework and Information modeling. AAS framework will develop how assets can communicate with other AASs and what communication devices will be used. On the other side, information modeling will be represented by sequence diagram to show how control flow and data flow in AAS  system. It is  created based on RAMI  4.0 layers. The communication protocol and data exchange type will be determined based on the relevance and compliance with simulation software used and convention in industry 4.0 community.

Since  this  research  proposes simulation  as  digital  twin  especially  using  Flexsim software, the  demonstrations are  needed to  show  the  main  advantages of  using  Flexsim software in digital twin system. Two demonstrations will be shown which are simulation-based optimization and creating dynamic dashboard.
In classical simulation, What-If analysis usually are used to get better decision. But it is less  effective  in  decision  making  so  that  nowadays optimization is  integrated  with  simulation. However, if the real condition is too dynamic, the decision needs to be taken fast and what-if analysis is more appropriate used rather than optimization. The process of simulation-based optimization in this research will follow iterative model [58]. Metaheuristic algorithm will give input parameters and simulation will use them to be simulated. Then the results will be given back to the algorithm. After that, metaheuristic algorithm will improve it and produce new input parameters. The process will be iterated until the number of iterations reached.

Metaheurisitic algorithm used in this research is Genetic Algorithm (GA) by following OptQuest optimizer [59]. The process of classical GA can be seen in Figure 3.3 [60]. Since optimizer is embedded in Flexsim, all parameters such as population size, crossover rate, and mutation rate have been fixed. There is no elitism strategy used in this original GA.

The scenario of simulation-based optimization in this research will be AGV capacity planning. The idea behind it is how many goods should be brought for each AGV so that it will maximize throughput and minimize energy usage simultaneously under uncertain conditions. Since the problem does not have an analytical closed-form so that it cannot be solved with classical  optimization technique or  mathematical programming  such as  calculus or  linear programming, then simulation is the one to calculate objective functions under uncertainties.

The trade-off in this AGV capacity planning problem is the more goods brought in one delivery, the  more energy  usage  needed for AGV  due to  the  more weight  and the  more loading/unloading time needed. Since there are 2 objectives, then multi-objective optimization is done by using Pareto Optimality approach. This approach will give a set of optimal solutions based on Non-dominated Sorting Genetic Algorithm II (NSGA-II) and users can choose based on their preferences. To select the single solution, Weighted Sum Method also will be used. The framework of simulation-based optimization for AGV Capacity Planning is  shown in Figure 3.4.

Conveyor will have another sensor in addition to speed sensor which is delivery path based on Semantic Product Memory (SemProM). Since warehouse will have some types of products, SemProM concept will be adopted to differ product types and object detector will recognize it. Object detector will be applied in every intersection of conveyor. This information is very important because digital twin needs to recognize which path in conveyor that each product type will go. This concept also will be applied in Cell-based Position storage rack since digital twin needs to recognize in which cell that a product type comes in and out. Object detector will be applied in each cell of rack and when product enters, data are sent to digital model. This  concept also should be applied in every starting point and ending point of the process so that digital model can recognize product that come in and come out.

After define AAS capability, AAS for each asset needs to be defined based on AAS structure. Later on, this structure will be applied in Automation Markup Language (AML) when the implementation stage is carried on. In this research, AAS template proposed by [49] is used. The result of AAS definition is shown in Table 4. 2. The structure of an AAS can be divided into a Digital Factory (DF) header and a DF body based on the concept of the DF framework benchmarked in International Electrotechnical Commission (IEC)  standard 62832 [9].  DF header describes a list  of I4.0-compliant properties or usually called manifest and DF body contains a component manager.

DF header consists of asset identifier (Asset ID) to differ each type of asset, AAS ID to differ every AAS even in the same asset family, for example AGV 1 and AGV 2 will  have different AAS ID even though they are the same asset, Number of Generic Submodels, and Number of Asset-Specific Submodels. Every ID must be unique to ensure that the information in  submodels can be located appropriately and communicated between AAS in a  common semantic manner so that interoperability can be realized.

Generic submodel in DF body means basic standardized submodel applicable to a broad variety  of  assets.  Every  AAS  must  include  generic  submodels  to  represent  mandatory information on assets. Index Data Item (IDI) submodel is the entry point of all of the other submodels which means that it is essentially a table of contents enabling efficient searching of all submodels. Property Value Statement (PVS) submodel contains metadata that allows users to discover the attributes of the asset such as names, versions, and also documentation. Some of  these  properties may  change along the  asset  lifecycle.  Hence, this  submodel must  be upgraded regularly. Communication (CM) submodel stores information about communication capabilities or communication protocol of the asset.

When  generic  submodel  informs  static  data,  contrarily  Asset-Specific  submodel informs dynamic data containing specific information about asset functions. Different assets require different submodels to reflect specialized functions. In this manner, considering the variety and complexity of each asset function, the number of asset-specific submodels differs. For  example, AGVs have speed submodel with real  value but operators do not  have this submodel. Operators will have position submodel with real value because digital model does not need to sense the speed of operators but needs to sense the position of operators. This determination depends on how the physical assets want to be reflected in digital twin.
