Digital  twin  should be  started  by  detailed  simulation  modeling.  Without  a  good simulation model, digital twin will not reflect physical system well. Before simulation model is created, the conceptual model of smart warehouse process should be clearly described first as  shown in  Figure  4. 2.  Layout design is  shown in  Figure  4. 3.  The flow of warehouse operations will be described as follows. When goods are arrived by truck, arrival goods will be received by forklift and goods will be sent to the Quality Control (QC) process. QC process will not generate waste products but it only checks the number and quality of products. Then, storage planning will  be done to  determine whether the goods will  be stored in

long-term storage or short-term storage. Short-term storage only stores the goods that will be sent in the same day, conversely long-term storage only stores the goods that will be sent in another day. After storage planning has been determined, Putaway process will be done by forklift either it comes from QC process to short-term storage or from long-term storage to short-term storage. When the pick-up time arrives, Order picking process is done by AGVs. AGVs will pick goods directly in short-term storage in their trajectory. The goods will be sent to shipping stage that consists of sorting and packaging process. Work in Process (WIP) from sorting process will be stored in the rack temporarily if the packaging process is not finished yet.

Digital  twin should not only enable one-direction flow from physical to digital asset (data flow), but it also should enable bi-direction flow from digital to physical asset (control flow). This research allows digital twin to control speed of AGV, capacity of AGV, and speed of conveyor as shown in Figure 4. 10. In addition, the most important point is the requirement part for simulation software. It should be fulfilled especially for connectivity issues. Flexsim allows OPC UA connection based on emulation tool so that control flow can be done and new parameters can be applied with simulated programmable logic controllers (PLC).

There are two modes in the emulation tool to  make a change which are Active and Inactive. Direct change should be checked as Active to make a change in real-time. This feature allows users to control physical assets directly from digital twin. Otherwise, it will not make a change if direct change mode is Inactive. Inactive mode option can be used whenever trial & error analysis or optimization is needed. After optimum parameter is  known, then it  can be applied with Active mode. It is worth noting that not all Flexsim versions can be used for digital twin purposes because of communication limitations especially for Flexsim under 2020 version that does not support OPC UA communication but it supports OPC DA and Modbus protocol. The configuration of sensors and controls also should be clearly defined in Flexsim based on AAS Capability as shown in Figure 4. 11. AAS needs system communication network to implement digital twin. Therefore, AAS network structure for a smart warehouse including the assets and data exchange paths is shown in Figure 4. 12. As stated before, in this research OPC UA and AML are used as main backbone communication between AAS. In simple words, AML will answer what data will be exchanged and OPC UA will answer how data are communicated.

There are 3 reasons why OPC UA and AML are chosen. First, OPC UA has been standardized in IEC 62541 and AML has been standardized in IEC 62714. Second, they are compatible with Flexsim software as digital model. Third, AML and OPC UA adhere to the I4.0 conventions and comply with the RAMI 4.0 model. In AAS system, each asset has a unique AAS ID. However, in terms of simplicity for representation, there are several numbers of the same assets like there are 5 AGVs in smart warehouse but it will only show one AGV in Figure 4. 12 because it will have similar AAS with other AGVs but different ID. This figure shows how AAS connects each other and what communication they use.

Take a  look  at  AGV  subsystem, there  will  be  speed sensor  and  speed controller connected with AGV through Universal Asynchronous Receiver-Transmitter (UART). There is also  position  sensor  to  sense  the  position  of  AGV  connected  through  radio  waves.  AGV  itself will be connected with Steering Control System through WiFi.  Steering Control System has capability to control speed, picking strategy such as AGV capacity, and route.
Steering Control System will be connected with Gateway through OPC UA. There are some gateways that can be used. One of them is LM Gateway201-OPC UA protocol. It supports wired and wireless protocols. The gateway has two functions which are data storage in AML and data exchange via OPC UA. From the gateway, it  will  connect with AAS of Flexsim through OPC UA and Flexsim will show real-time condition through external interface.

The interaction between AAS is  shown as a sequence diagram in Figure  4. 13 that represents the dynamic information flow and control flow across the digitalized network of AASs by following RAMI 4.0 layers. First, the AML-related OPC UA server will be initialized. Then, OPC UA sessions will be created with different clients which are OPC UA Client from AAS of Flexsim and OPC UA Interface from AAS of Field devices. Control flows are then generated by the users from AAS Flexsim and passed down to the AASs of the field devices. Here, warehousing tasks are executed according to the control strategy. Feedback parameters are then given back to the AAS of Flexsim. Thus, the digital twin system operates in a loop.

chunks.text: AGV takes crucial part in smart warehouse operation. It brings goods from storage to the shipping area and it has their own trajectory. Capacity of AGV determines total throughput and energy usage since AGV uses electricity energy in their operation. However, the more goods carried out, the heavier they are that takes longer loading & unloading time and the more energy usage needed. Therefore, there is trade-off in this problem. Even tough there are some objectives also that can be considered such as optimizing the route of AGV and the utilization of worker in warehouse, but only total throughput and energy usage will  be considered here since those objectives influence the customer satisfaction, profit, and operation cost directly.

It cannot be denied that monitoring and controlling is the key to make good decisions in operation. This is  the main purpose of industry 4.0 as well that can be achieved through digital twin technology. Therefore, the dashboard is one of the tools that can be used. This is useful  to  detect  problems  with  visualization  rather  than  numbers.  Through  simulation technology, the dashboard can be very accurate and real-time as well. Hence, dashboard for smart warehouse is created by using Flexsim simulation software feature for some important parameters such as total throughput, Forklift State, Operator State, and AGV Utilization. However longer traveling does not mean higher energy usage, but it depends also with how many loads that AGV brings per travel. The new concept of simulation-based digital twin based on Asset Administration Shell (AAS) framework has been proposed by using Flexsim software with smart warehouse as a use-case. Asset-specific submodels also have been proposed for Automated Guided Vehicle (AGV),  Operator,  Conveyor, Forklift,  and  Storage  Rack.  AAS  capability  also  has  been designed which digital twin is able to monitor and control the real system as well as providing optimization. It  needs OPC  UA  and AutomationML as  communication protocol and data exchange type between AAS.
The verified simulation model imitating smart warehouse has been constructed as well built in Flexsim software. It has imitated the main assets in smart warehouse as well as the layout and logic behind it. System integration architecture also has been proposed through AAS framework and sequence diagram to help the understanding on how data and control flow from all AASs including AAS of Flexsim as digital twin.

Since this research proposes simulation with Flexsim software as digital twin, two main advantages have been demonstrated. The result of simulation-based optimization for multiobjective AGV capacity planning shows that in order to maximize the total throughput and minimize energy usage simultaneously, solution ID 95 gives optimum result where the capacity for each AGV is as follows: AGV 1 (X1) = 9, AGV 2 (X2) = 9, AGV 3 (X3) = 9, AGV 4 (X4) = 8, AGV 5 (X5) = 9. This is going to be breakthrough for Digital Twin research since previous state-of-the-art analysis about DT stated that even there are still  lack of DT that can reflect optimization. The  result  of designing  dynamic dashboard  also has  been demonstrated to increase the capability and accuracy of controlling and monitoring such as total throughput for each product type, AGV Utilization, and Operator State.
4.

Recommendation will be given for two stakeholders, namely smart warehouse and further work as follows:
1. Recommendation for smart warehouse
Smart  warehouse has not only a lot  of assets but also movable assets that need to be analyzed carefully. This is because warehouse is an important entity in logistics. In order to enhance  smart warehouse  operation,  system  integration through  digital twin establishment based on  AAS  framework is  very appropriate to  be  implemented, this research is a starting point to implement digital twin as the basic technology for system integration. Two-stage DT application has been done in this research which are system design of AAS and simulation modeling. Other warehouses also can use this proposed concept as well  as methodology for establishing simulation-based digital twin that  has been constructed in this  research and start  to  apply 2 next stages  which are  hardware installation and PLC programming to connect digital assets and physical assets based on the proposed communication protocol.
2. Recommendation for further work

In  reality, there are still  many lacks  of industry 4.0 scenario application especially in system integration. Moreover, there is still a few researches working on AAS as the key of integration and standardization. Since this research contributes in proposing simulation model especially Flexsim  software as dynamic digital twin  and have tried to  consider assets a wider area, further work can start to research in the implementation stage and find efficient way. Economic analysis also should be considered in order to achieve minimum cost in implementing digital twin. Until today, it is still hard to establish standard manner to deploy digital  twin without AAS.  Later on, a lot of industries cannot be integrated. Without standardization, each industry will have its own digital twin and each industry will stand by itself without any integration and communication between them. That is not what industry 4.0 targeted. Moreover, this proposed concept also can be integrated with data analytics by using the same AAS framework with some additional submodels. Some of data will be sent to the simulation that will be used as monitoring and controlling based on optimized decision and others will  be  stored in  the cloud as  big  data to

establish predictive maintenance and give the control to the physical asset automatically. Digital twin from simulation also can be extended into AR or VR to enhance its capability. Thus, industry 4.0 scenarios can be integrated systematically and comprehensively.
